11.evidence_source: The text describes a single analysis examining mediation effects, referring to 'the final model' and 'the data set', indicating one study.
11._section_summary: This section details a mediation analysis investigating body appreciation as a mediator between various psychological constructs (discrepancy perfectionism, order perfectionism, attachment anxiety, restrictive/critical caregiver eating messages) and intuitive eating. The study utilized Shrout and Bolger's (2002) bootstrap procedures with 1000 samples to estimate indirect effects and confidence intervals. Results indicated that body appreciation fully mediated the link from discrepancy perfectionism to intuitive eating, and partially mediated the links from attachment anxiety and caregiver eating messages to intuitive eating, while the indirect effect from order perfectionism was not significant.

12.evidence_source: The text consistently refers to 'In this study, we explored a model' and 'our model', indicating a single study.
12._section_summary: This discussion section summarizes the findings of a single study that explored a model of positive body image, specifically body appreciation, in college women. The model investigated interpersonal and intrapersonal factors influencing body appreciation and its connections to intuitive eating and depressive symptoms. Key findings include body appreciation's mediational role in the link between maladaptive perfectionism and intuitive eating, and its partial mediation for attachment anxiety and restrictive/critical caregiver eating messages to intuitive eating. The study also identified barriers and facilitators to body appreciation and predictors of discrepancy perfectionism.

13.evidence_source: The section consistently refers to "this study's limitations" and "this study", indicating a single study.
13._section_summary: This section discusses the limitations of the study and offers directions for future research. Key limitations include the correlational nature of the data, which prevents causal interpretations, potential recall and measurement errors due to self-reported data (e.g., BMI), and the homogeneity of the sample, which consisted mainly of White, young adult, first-year college women. The authors suggest future research should investigate the model in more diverse populations, including men.

14.evidence_source: The text consistently refers to "Our final model" and "this study" (singular), indicating a single study.
14._section_summary: This conclusion section summarizes the findings of a single study, noting that the final model, which investigated interpersonal and intrapersonal links to body appreciation and its connection to intuitive eating, fit well with college women. Body appreciation was found to play a central mediational role, linking interpersonal (restrictive/critical caregiver eating messages, attachment anxiety) and intrapersonal (discrepancy perfectionism) variables to intuitive eating. The study also found that body appreciation did not predict unique variance in depressive symptoms, suggesting it is distinct from negative body image, and recommends exploring similar models with diverse samples.
